subject: Cooking
title: Expiration Dates Are Mostly Made Up
description: A fast breakdown of Expiration Dates Are Mostly Made Up for builders.

hook.text: Americans throw away $161 billion of food per year based on expiration dates. Most of it is still safe.

buildup.text: 'Best by,' 'sell by,' and 'use by' dates are set by manufacturers — not safety regulators.

discovery.text: These dates indicate peak quality, not safety. Canned food can last years past its printed date.

twist.text: Infant formula is the only product with a federally regulated expiration date in the US.

climax.text: The USDA confirms that foods past 'best by' dates are usually safe — smell, appearance, and texture are better guides.

punchline.text: Expiration dates protect brand reputation, not your health.

quiz.question: What is the only US food product with a federally regulated expiration date?

details.summary: Most expiration dates indicate peak quality, not safety. Infant formula is the only US product with a federally regulated expiration date. Sell-by and best-by labeling is inconsistent and causes massive food waste — an estimated 30 percent of food is discarded while still perfectly safe to eat.
details.whyItMatters: Misunderstanding date labels is the leading cause of household food waste. Recognizing that most dates are manufacturer suggestions, not safety deadlines, could prevent billions of dollars in wasted food.
takeaways: Best-by dates indicate quality, not safety for most products
Sell-by dates tell stores when to rotate stock, not consumers
Misread date labels cause up to 20 percent of consumer food waste

faq.question: Which dates should you actually follow?
faq.answer: Take use-by dates on deli meats, soft cheeses, and ready-to-eat foods seriously — these can harbor Listeria. Infant formula dates are legally enforced. For most pantry items, canned goods, and dry products, best-by dates are quality guidelines.

faq.question: How long do common foods last past their dates?
faq.answer: Canned goods last years past their date. Dry pasta and rice are fine for months to years. Eggs stay fresh 3 to 5 weeks after purchase. Hard cheese lasts weeks past its date with mold trimmed. Yogurt is usually fine a week or two past its date in the refrigerator.
